text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- BNDES WILL TRY TO SALE CVRD TODAY

Brazilian officials today will try to sale state mining company CVRD, whose auction has been delayed since last Tuesday due to a host of legal challenges. Officials say a favorable court ruling yesterday should pave the way for an auction today at the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.
-- LEASING LIKELY TO GROW AS RESULT OF IOF TAX HIKES
The increase in the IOF financial tax on consumer credit operations, from six percent to 15 percent, should lead to an increase in leasing, which was not affected by the tax hike.
-- THREE BOYS KILL GIRL, THEN SEXUALLY ABUSE HER BODY
Three boys aged nine, 10 and 13, have confessed to killing a 10-year-old girl and then using a broomstick to sexually abuse her body.
--RETAILERS UP CREDIT TO COUNTERACT HIGHER IOF TAX

Retailers are increasing credit to consumers to compensate for an increase in the IOF financial tax on consumer credit operations. Merchants say they will keep prices the same and offer promotions for the Mothers' Day holiday on May 11.
-- TELESP REOPENS SUBSCRIPTIONS FOR CELLULAR LINES

Sao Paulo state telephone company Telesp today will once again accept applications for up to two million cellular telephone lines and will also announce the opening up of the digital system to the private sector to create 600,000 new cellular lines by 1998.

Thirteen inmates were holding 18 guards hostage at the House of Detention in Sao Paulo. According to one hostage, the inmates are drug addicts who cannot pay their debts to suppliers within the prison.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
